annotation_description: Played Bloodstained Mire instead of Fiery Islet, missing the opportunity to cast Preordain on turn 1. message: Select a Swamp or Mountain card
annotation_description: Fetching a basic Mountain instead of Steam Vents means the player cannot cast Preordain this turn, since they have no blue mana source on the battlefield. With Preordain in hand and wanting to sculpt draws early, having access to blue mana immediately is important. Steam Vents (paying 2 life) would provide both blue and red mana, enabling Preordain to be cast this turn. The player already has Fiery Islet in hand which could provide red/blue later, but getting Steam Vents now allows immediate Preordain casting with the Fiery Islet as a backup land drop.

With two fetch lands in hand (Arid Mesa and Bloodstained Mire), targeting yourself with Mishra's Bauble is significantly more valuable because you can see the top card of your own library and then decide whether to crack a fetch to shuffle it away before the Bauble's delayed draw trigger resolves at your next upkeep. This gives a pseudo-scry effect. Targeting the opponent provides information but no actionable way to change outcomes.

Playing Verdant Catacombs instead of Forest + Delighted Halfling delays the mana dork by a turn, slowing the curve significantly. With Forest + Halfling on turn 1, the player can cast Agatha's Soul Cauldron on turn 2 and potentially Yawgmoth on turn 3 (using Halfling's legendary mana ability). Playing just a fetchland wastes the opportunity to deploy the key accelerant.

Fetching a Swamp instead of a Forest means Delighted Halfling cannot be cast this turn, losing a critical turn 1 mana dork. With Halfling able to produce any color for the legendary Yawgmoth, early black mana is less urgent than deploying the mana accelerant on turn 1.

Fetching a basic Swamp instead of Overgrown Tomb is suboptimal. With Delighted Halfling in hand (which needs G to cast on turn 1), Dryad Arbor available, and Agatha's Soul Cauldron + Yawgmoth in hand, the player needs both black and green mana. Overgrown Tomb (paying 2 life to enter untapped) provides both B and G, giving much more flexibility. A basic Swamp only provides B. The player already has Dryad Arbor and a Forest in hand for green, but Overgrown Tomb is strictly better here since it opens up more sequencing options in future turns (e.g., casting Delighted Halfling off the dual land if needed, or having access to both colors from a single land). The Verdant Catacombs was already fetching, so getting a dual land maximizes mana flexibility.

The player has a Delighted Halfling in hand and a Swamp in play, but no green mana to cast it. However, they also have a Forest in hand and a Dryad Arbor. They should play the Forest this turn (they haven't played a land yet) to have green mana available, then cast Delighted Halfling. This would set up turn 3 Yawgmoth via Halfling + Forest + Swamp (using Halfling's legendary mana ability for one of Yawgmoth's colored costs). Instead, they passed without playing a land or doing anything, wasting an entire turn's worth of development. Even if they didn't want to cast Walking Ballista for X=0, they should have at minimum played their Forest land drop.

With a Swamp in play and a Forest in hand, casting Walking Ballista for X=0 (free) would put a 0/0 artifact creature onto the battlefield. While it dies immediately as a 0/0, it goes to the graveyard where it can later be exiled by Agatha's Soul Cauldron to grant its activated abilities to other creatures. This is a key combo piece in the Yawgmoth deck - Cauldron exiling Ballista lets any creature with a +1/+1 counter ping for damage by removing the counter, enabling the Yawgmoth combo loop. Playing Ballista for 0 now puts it in the graveyard for free, setting up the Cauldron combo. However, the player declined to cast either copy.

Playing Bloodstained Mire as the land drop before activating Mishra's Bauble is a minor sequencing error. Mishra's Bauble can look at the top card of your own library, which is relevant information before deciding whether to crack a fetchland (fetches shuffle your library). By playing the fetch first, you lose the option to Bauble yourself, see what's on top, and then decide whether to shuffle it away with the fetch. Additionally, casting Preordain (which scrys 2) before playing a fetchland would be ideal sequencing - you scry cards to the top and don't want to shuffle them away. The optimal line is likely: activate Mishra's Bauble targeting yourself, then cast Preordain off the Mountain, then play the land for turn. However, since Preordain costs U and they only have a Mountain, they can't cast Preordain this turn without fetching first. Still, they could have activated Bauble first to see the top card, then decided on sequencing.

Cracking Bloodstained Mire before activating Mishra's Bauble loses a small information advantage. Bauble could have revealed the top card of the library, and if it was undesirable, then fetching would shuffle it away. If it was good, they could keep it on top and fetch later or not at all.

The player declined to cast Walking Ballista for X=0 (free) which would put a 0/0 artifact creature onto the battlefield. While it dies immediately as a 0/0, it goes to the graveyard where it can be exiled by Agatha's Soul Cauldron to grant its activated abilities to other creatures with +1/+1 counters. With 3 mana available (Swamp, Forest, Delighted Halfling), playing a second Delighted Halfling is suboptimal. The key card in hand is Agatha's Soul Cauldron (costs 2), which is a critical combo piece that enables the Walking Ballista + Yawgmoth combo. Playing Badgermole Cub for 1G would be better - it's a 2/2 body that earthbends a land into a creature (providing an extra sacrifice target for Yawgmoth) and generates extra green mana when tapping creatures. This accelerates the combo plan more effectively. Alternatively, casting Agatha's Soul Cauldron this turn (for 2 mana) would set up the combo engine immediately. Playing a redundant legendary Delighted Halfling (one will be sacrificed to legend rule... wait, no - Delighted Halfling is not legendary). Still, the second Halfling provides only 1 extra mana next turn, while Badgermole Cub provides a body + earthbend creature + mana acceleration, or Cauldron directly advances the combo. Actually, with Delighted Halfling producing any color for legendary spells, playing the second Halfling means next turn you'd have access to potentially 5+ mana to cast Yawgmoth. But casting Agatha's Soul Cauldron now (2 mana from Swamp + Forest) while still having Halfling untapped to play Badgermole Cub would also work - wait, Cub costs 1G. So the line would be: tap Swamp + Forest for Cauldron, then tap Halfling for colorless... can't cast anything else meaningful. Playing Badgermole Cub (1G from Forest + Halfling) leaves Swamp open. Next turn with earthbent land + Dryad Arbor + Swamp + Cub's mana bonus, you could have enough for Yawgmoth. The Cub line seems strongest as it creates an extra creature for Yawgmoth sacrificing and adds mana.

Casting Walking Ballista for X=1 (a 1/1) instead of Badgermole Cub is suboptimal. Badgermole Cub is a 2/2 that also earthbends a land into a creature with a +1/+1 counter (creating an additional body/mana source) and provides extra green mana when tapping creatures. This significantly accelerates toward casting Yawgmoth next turn. A 1/1 Walking Ballista is fragile and provides minimal board impact. With Yawgmoth in hand as the key card to deploy on turn 4, maximizing mana development with Badgermole Cub is clearly better. The Ballista can be deployed later when more mana is available or when the Soul Cauldron combo is online.

Casting Walking Ballista for X=1 (a fragile 1/1) instead of Badgermole Cub, which would provide a 2/2 body, earthbend a land into a creature with a +1/+1 counter, and generate extra green mana from all creature taps (Delighted Halflings, Dryad Arbor, the earthbent land). Badgermole Cub would likely enable casting Yawgmoth as early as turn 4 by dramatically increasing mana production.

Gem25P Gramps has three creatures that could attack (two Delighted Halflings and Dryad Arbor) against an opponent with no creatures to block. The opponent only has a Mountain, Fiery Islet, and Mishra's Bauble on board — no blockers whatsoever. Attacking with all three would deal 3 damage for free (1+1+1), bringing the opponent from 18 to 15. There is no downside to attacking here since there are no blockers and no combat tricks to worry about. The Delighted Halflings aren't needed for mana this turn since Gem25P Gramps likely wants to cast Agatha's Soul Cauldron (2 mana, can use the Swamp + one Halfling or Dryad Arbor) and still attack with the remaining creatures. Even if one Halfling is needed for mana, the other Halfling and Dryad Arbor could attack for 2 free damage.

GPT4om Coach chose to look at the opponent's top card with Mishra's Bauble instead of their own, missing the well-known Bauble + fetchland synergy. With Arid Mesa in hand (unplayed), looking at their own top card would let them decide whether to crack Arid Mesa to shuffle away a bad card, effectively giving them a scry effect.

Attacking with all creatures, including mana dorks, is problematic when Gem25P Gramps has Yawgmoth, Thran Physician (2BB) and Agatha's Soul Cauldron (2) in hand that need to be cast soon. The opponent has no blockers (only lands and a Mishra's Bauble), so there's no board presence to pressure. By tapping all creatures to attack, Gramps loses the ability to tap Delighted Halflings and Dryad Arbor for mana in the second main phase. With Swamp + Forest + 2 Delighted Halflings + Dryad Arbor available (5 mana sources), Gramps could cast Yawgmoth (2BB using Delighted Halfling for uncounterable legendary) or Agatha's Soul Cauldron + Badgermole Cub this turn. Instead, by attacking with all three creatures, only Swamp and Forest are untapped for post-combat plays, leaving just 2 mana available. Dealing 3 damage is far less impactful than deploying a key combo piece like Yawgmoth or Cauldron a turn earlier.

Casting Slickshot Show-Off during postcombat main phase wastes its haste ability - it can't attack this turn. The player should have plotted it instead (paying the same 1R) to cast it for free next turn during precombat main, getting a full attack with it. Alternatively, they could have cast it precombat to attack immediately. Additionally, casting Slickshot before Preordain or playing Arid Mesa is poor sequencing - they should play land first and cast the sorcery before committing the creature.

Attacking with both Delighted Halflings and Dryad Arbor taps out all mana creatures. Gem25P Gramps has Agatha's Soul Cauldron (2 mana), Yawgmoth (2BB), Walking Ballista, and Badgermole Cub in hand. By attacking with all mana producers, they lose the ability to cast anything meaningful in their second main phase. The opponent has Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying with haste) which can't block any ground creatures anyway, so attacking with Dryad Arbor is fine, but tapping both Delighted Halflings means losing access to 2 mana post-combat. With Misty Rainforest still available to crack, they have at most 3 mana post-combat (Swamp, Forest, Misty fetch). Keeping one Halfling back would allow casting Agatha's Soul Cauldron post-combat while still dealing 2 damage (Dryad Arbor + one Halfling). The 1 extra damage from the second Halfling (total 3 vs 2) is marginal compared to the flexibility of having mana available.

Cast Preordain before playing Arid Mesa as their land for the turn. Playing Arid Mesa first (and potentially cracking it) would thin the deck before Preordain's scry 2, giving marginally better card selection. Additionally, having the land in play first ensures maximum mana availability for the rest of the turn.

Preordain's scry targets your own library to set up draws. Looking at the opponent's library with Preordain's 'select a player' is not how Preordain works - but this appears to be a Mishra's Bauble activation or Preordain scry target selection. Actually, reviewing more carefully: the stack shows Preordain resolving, and the message says 'Select a player.' Preordain says 'Scry 2, then draw a card' - it doesn't ask you to select a player. This must be Mishra's Bauble's ability ('Look at the top card of target player's library'). Looking at the opponent's library with Mishra's Bauble is generally correct since you already know your own top cards (especially after Preordain scry). This is actually a reasonable play - choosing to look at the opponent's library gives you information you don't have.

The reasoning says to play Verdant Catacombs as the land drop first, but the actual action taken was casting Yawgmoth, Thran Physician without first playing the land. Playing Verdant Catacombs first would thin the deck and provide an additional land on the battlefield. With Delighted Halfling available to make Yawgmoth uncounterable and provide colored mana, the sequencing should be: play Verdant Catacombs, crack it for a land, then tap lands/Halflings to cast Yawgmoth. By casting Yawgmoth first (presumably using both Halflings + other lands), Gramps misses the opportunity to have the extra land from the fetch available this turn, which could matter for casting additional spells like Badgermole Cub or Walking Ballista with the remaining mana. However, with the opponent tapped out at 10 life, this is a relatively low-impact sequencing error.

Targeted opponent's Delighted Halfling with Mutagenic Growth instead of their own Slickshot Show-Off. This wastes the +2/+2 buff entirely, giving it to an opponent's creature instead of their flying attacker. With Yawgmoth about to resolve, maximizing damage with Slickshot Show-Off is critical.

annotation_description: Fetched Overgrown Tomb and paid 2 life (going to 13) against a burn/prowess deck when already having Swamp + Overgrown Tomb for black mana sources. Against Slickshot Show-Off and likely burn spells, every point of life matters.

This wastes 2 life (Phyrexian mana cost) while actively helping the opponent, and misses a significant damage opportunity with the flying Slickshot.

Adding +2/+2 to Slickshot would make it a 5/4 flyer (or more with additional spells), representing massive flying damage against an opponent at 12 life. Against a Yawgmoth combo deck, the burn/aggro player needs to maximize damage output to race the combo.

GPT4om Coach is casting Mutagenic Growth (likely paying 2 life, going to 8) and targeting Delighted Halfling — an opponent's creature that is tapped and not attacking. This wastes the Mutagenic Growth for absolutely no benefit. The only friendly creature on their board is Slickshot Show-Off, which would benefit enormously from the +2/+2 buff (and would also trigger its +2/+0 ability since Mutagenic Growth is a noncreature spell, making it effectively +4/+2). With Slickshot Show-Off being a flying hasty threat, buffing it before combat could deal significant damage or even threaten lethal with additional spells.

GPT4om Coach is casting Mutagenic Growth (likely paying 2 life, going from 10 to 8) and targeting Dryad Arbor instead of their own Slickshot Show-Off. Mutagenic Growth on Slickshot Show-Off would give it +2/+2 AND trigger its ability for an additional +2/+0, making it a 5/4 flyer. Instead, pumping the opponent's Dryad Arbor accomplishes nothing useful - it makes an opponent's creature bigger. This is either a misclick or a fundamental misunderstanding. The only scenario where this might make sense is if they're trying to save Dryad Arbor from dying to set up some interaction, but there's no reason to help the opponent's creature.

Mutagenic Growth is one of the strongest cards in hand for a Slickshot Show-Off burst kill. It's a free spell (+2/+2 plus Slickshot's +2/+0 trigger = +4 damage for just 2 life). Against Yawgmoth's grinding engine, the Slickshot player needs to assemble a lethal burst turn quickly, and Mutagenic Growth is critical to that plan.

The +1/+1 counter on Ballista could potentially wait or the mana could be better used for developing the board.

Only attacked with Walking Ballista (likely 1 damage) instead of also attacking with Yawgmoth, Thran Physician (2/4). Even with Lava Dart's flashback (sacrifice Mountain) for a second point, 2 total damage still doesn't kill a 2/4. This completely wastes the Lava Dart's damage output.

Gem25P Gramps is at 12 life with the opponent at 7 life. Looking at the board, Gramps has Delighted Halfling (1/2), Dryad Arbor (1/1), Yawgmoth (2/4), and Walking Ballista available to attack. The opponent has only Slickshot Show-Off (1/2 flying) as a potential blocker. Casting Dragon's Rage Channeler before playing a land is a sequencing error. GPT4om Coach has multiple land options in hand (Arid Mesa, Wooded Foothills, Steam Vents) and should play a land first to ensure the land drop isn't missed. More importantly, casting DRC before combat means the opponent sees the creature and can plan accordingly, whereas leading with a land drop (especially a fetch land) preserves options. Additionally, if the plan is to attack with Slickshot Show-Off and cast noncreature spells to pump it, casting a creature spell first doesn't trigger Slickshot's ability. The correct sequence would be to play a land first (like Wooded Foothills or Arid Mesa, which can be cracked later for deck thinning and delirium), then consider whether to cast creatures before or after combat based on what spells are available to pump Slickshot.

Attacking with Yawgmoth, Delighted Halfling, and Dryad Arbor would push through meaningful damage. Even if Slickshot blocks Yawgmoth and DRC blocks one small creature, at least 1-2 damage gets through, putting opponent closer to lethal range for Walking Ballista pings or Yawgmoth drain.

Gem25P Gramps has Walking Ballista on the battlefield (likely with at least 1 +1/+1 counter), Yawgmoth, Thran Physician, and multiple creatures including Dryad Arbor and Delighted Halfling. The opponent is at 5 life. With Yawgmoth's ability (pay 1 life, sacrifice a creature to draw a card and put a -1/-1 counter on a creature), combined with Walking Ballista's ability to remove counters to deal damage, plus Young Wolf in hand (which has undying for repeated sacrifice loops), there is very likely a line to deal lethal damage this turn. Even without a full combo kill, Walking Ballista can ping the opponent, and Yawgmoth can sacrifice creatures to draw into more resources or directly pressure the opponent's life total. Declining to activate any abilities during combat when the opponent is at 5 life and you have powerful sacrifice/damage outlets available is a critical missed opportunity.
